# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Intake Brief — Herdr extension unresponsive on larger worklog databases (WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Work Items pane freezes or visibly lags when it refreshes, is slow to
initially appear, and is slow to reflect some changes after agent writes —
problems that scale with the size of the worklog database. On a ~100 MB /
2,600-item worklog the pane's refresh path still spawns slow, memory-hungry
`wl` CLI processes (`wl worklist` ≈ 1 s / 1.2 MB JSON cold; `wl list` subsets
0.5–0.9 s each peaking ~130–145 MB; per-expand `wl dep list` ≈ 0.4 s) and the
auto-sync may spawn a ~36 s `wl sync` every 60 s. Recent fixes (event-driven
refresh, consolidated `wl worklist`, hydrator timeouts) improved the picture but
the extension remains sluggish — "improved but still not good enough".

## Users (example user stories)

- **Agent operators running the Herdr Work Items pane** — the primary user.
  - *As an operator, when the pane auto-refreshes, I want the UI to stay
    responsive (no multi-second freezes, keystrokes accepted promptly) so my
    monitoring flow is uninterrupted.*
  - *As an operator on a large worklog, when an agent writes to a work item, I
    want the pane to reflect the change within a couple of seconds so I can
    trust the list is current.*
  - *As an operator, I want the pane to open promptly and not feel like the
    extension is a drag on my machine even at 100 MB+ worklog scale.*

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Pane stays responsive during refresh:** a default-view refresh does not block the TUI event loop for more than ~200 ms of perceived lag in aggregate (verified with an automated test harness or measured timing on a large fixture DB) — keystrokes/commands process promptly while a refresh is in flight.
- **Single-figure refresh cost on large DBs:** a default-view refresh end-to-end (event → data load → render) is bounded to ≤ ~1.5 s wall-clock p95 on a DB of ~2,600 items / ~100 MB, including per-expand child fetches; the consolidated `wl worklist` single-read path stays the norm — no regression to multi-spawn refreshes.
- **Auto-sync cannot stall the pane:** while a long `wl sync` (measured ~36 s on the 100 MB DB) is in flight in the background, the pane remains responsive — no lock wait, no event-loop stall, at most a brief non-blocking status notice.
- **Change reflection latency:** after a `wl` write, the pane reflects the change within ~2 s p95 via the event-driven watch path at large-DB scale.
- **Reduced memory footprint:** a refresh's spawned `wl` processes peak at no more than a documented per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB/spawn observed baseline, OR concurrent spawns are bounded so aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g. ≤ ~300 MB).
- **No regressions:** the full Herdr plugin + TUI test suites pass; the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and event-driven watch semantics are preserved.
## Constraints

- Must preserve the existing event-driven refresh, in-process SQLite read
  scopes, consolidated `wl worklist` single-read default view, and
  zero-spawn-when-idle guarantees (documented in
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`).
- Must not change the hydrator's core behaviour or the scheduler's sequential
  dispatch model without a separate work item.
- Fixes must target "large worklog" scale (100 MB+/2,600+ items) without
  regressing small worklogs.
- No new heavy dependencies; prefer reuse of the existing in-process SQLite
  read path (`@worklog/shared` `WorklogDatabase`) over new spawns.

## Existing state (measured)

- `.worklog/worklog.db` ≈ 109 MB, ~2,631 items, read cache 81 MB / ~709 entries
  (this repo).
- `wl worklist --json`: ≈ 1.0 s cold, ~1.2 MB payload.
- `wl list` (each of the four subsets): 0.5–0.9 s, peak ~130–145 MB RSS.
- `wl next`: ≈ 0.6 s. `wl dep list`: ≈ 0.4 s per call.
- `wl sync`: ≈ 36 s on this DB; auto-sync spawns fire-and-forget every 60 s
  (single-flight + heartbeat skip across panes).
- Herdr pane refresh: 30 s auto tick + event-driven (≤ ~150 ms debounce),
  single consolidated `wl worklist` read for the default view; in-process
  SQLite reads for actionable counts / child fetches within a refresh scope.
- Previous unresponsiveness work completed: WL-0MMNZWOZ60M8JY6E (TUI
  unresponsive, critical), WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P (hydrate timeouts), WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN (snappy event-driven refresh), WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6 (wl next perf), WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR (background task runtime), WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S / WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG (memoization + in-process reads), WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78 (consolidated worklist read).

## Desired change

Investigate the remaining large-DB cost drivers in the Herdr refresh path and
shave them down to the acceptance criteria above. Known candidates (to confirm
during implementation):

1. **Auto-sync `wl sync` cost (~36 s):** profile why `wl sync` is so slow on a
   100 MB DB (git operations, JSONL export, DB compaction?) and either bound it
   or restructure so the pane never waits on / competes with it.
2. **`wl list`/`wl worklist` RSS (~130–145 MB/spawn):** confirm where the
   memory goes (full JSON materialisation? enrichments?) and consider streaming
   or trimming payloads; cap concurrent spawns.
3. **Per-expand `wl dep list` / `wl list --parent` spawns:** replace with
   in-process SQLite reads (via the existing refresh scope) so expanding nodes
   doesn't spawn more slow processes.
4. **Event-loop blocking:** ensure every remaining spawn is off the TUI event
   loop and each refresh's in-process SQLite work stays within the one-open
   refresh scope (no per-helper DB opens).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — consolidated worklist read, in-process
  read scope, CLI exec/timeouts, spawn cap.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — background `wl sync` spawn/heartbeat.
- `src/sync.ts` / `src/commands/sync.ts` — `wl sync` pipeline (JSONL export,
  git push) — the main suspected ~36 s cost.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — refresh orchestration, guarded refresh,
  child-fetch on expand.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — the consolidated read command (payload size).
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — list/query paths used by these reads.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — per-item `wl dep list` calls (bounded by
  hydrator timeout work but still per-item spawns).

## Related work

- **WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P** — Hydrate task timeouts cause HERDR UI to become
  unresponsive (completed, high) — parent context for UI responsiveness.
- **WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN** — Make Herdr UI refresh snappy after agent work-item
  updates (completed, high) — event-driven refresh; AC 4 re-verification.
- **WL-0MNAGHQ33005BVY6** — TUI slow-down investigation (completed).
- **WL-0MMNZWOZ60M8JY6E** — TUI unresponsive to keyboard input (completed,
  critical).
- **WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6** — Investigate wl next performance bottlenecks
  (completed, high).
- **WL-0MSNIX4V60012266** — Compress herdr plugin meta-data (completed) —
  vertical space, not to be confused with data-size perf.
- **WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR** — Background Task Runtime for non-blocking ops
  (completed, high).
- **WL-0MT1KJNGA006EEHU** — Memory pressure monitoring (completed, high).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the ~36 s `wl sync` is dominated by git push/network or JSONL
  export; fixing it may belong to a separate `wl sync` perf item (scope-creep
  guard: record a linked child, don't absorb).
- **Risk:** memory-per-spawn may be inherent to the current `better-sqlite3` +
  full-JSON payload; trimming payloads could change the fetcher contract —
  needs care to preserve the documented `wl worklist` payload stability.
- **Risk:** in-process SQLite reads on a 100 MB DB can themselves be slow
  (open + FTS DDL ~46–70 ms); the one-open-per-refresh scope must be kept.
- **Assumption:** the operator's "large DB" ≈ 100–200 MB / 2,600+ items
  (ContextHub's own scale) per Q2 answer; ACs are framed at that scale.
- **Assumption:** perceived responsiveness is driven by (a) refresh blocking
  and (b) write→reflect latency, per Q1/Q3 answers.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What does 'unresponsive' mean in practice?" — Answer (operator):
  "(a) The Work Items pane freezes/lags visibly when it refreshes — UI stutters
  or misses keystrokes for seconds", plus freeform "slow to reflect some
  changes" (b). Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Approximately how large is the worklog database where you see this?" —
  Answer (operator): "(a) Similar to ContextHub's own (≈2–3k items, 100 MB+
  worklog.db)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Is this a new recurrence after the recent fixes…?" — Answer (operator):
  "Improved but still not good enough" (b). Source: interactive reply.
- Research: measured on this repo's own `.worklog` (109 MB db, 2,631 items);
  timings listed under "Existing state". Prior-work links in "Related work".

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MN53B6B1071X95T** – Epic: Fix TUI Freezing Issues (completed)
- **WL-0MUEK7H39008VVUF** – Ship guard always reports 'Cannot verify pane state': wl list --json (8.5 MB) exceeds the 8 MB maxBuffer (completed)
- **WL-0MPGV61D0006SE7K** – TUI list adapter drops items because wl list JSON is wrapped (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mv02va29009wben, 60s, auto, becomes, cache, call, cause, cold, completed, consolidated, context, contexthub, database, default, dep, determined, driven, entries, event, every, extension, fire, forget, herdr, high, hydrate, intake, json, large, list, memory, next, pane, perf, prior, priority, queries, read, refresh, repo, reported, root, scope, seed, spawn, subset, sync, syncs, task, timeouts, tui, updates, via, view, when, worklist
- `CLI.md` — matched: auto, cache, call, cause, cold, completed, consolidated, context, database, default, dep, driven, entries, especially, event, every, extension, herdr, high, intake, json, large, list, memory, next, pane, perf, prior, priority, queries, read, refresh, repo, reported, root, scope, spawn, subset, sync, syncs, task, tui, updates, via, view, when, worklist
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0muy0rdbq001h74p, 0mv02va29009wben, 60s, auto, cache, call, cause, completed, context, contexthub, database, default, dep, entries, event, every, extension, fire, herdr, high, intake, json, large, list, memory, monitoring, next, pane, perf, prior, priority, read, refresh, repo, root, spawn, sync, syncs, task, tui, updates, via, view, when, worklist

# F7 — Large-DB responsiveness verification at scale

## Background

The parent's ACs are acceptance criteria for the whole pane behaviour at scale.
F1–F6 each deliver targeted fixes and tests; this item is the end-to-end
verification slice that confirms every parent AC holds together on a
~2,600-item / ~100 MB fixture after all changes, including the AC 4
write→reflect re-verification (extending WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN to large-DB
scale) and AC 6's full-suite no-regression gate.

## Target outcome

One reproducible end-to-end evidence run (documented commands + test suite)
that every parent acceptance criterion 1–6 is met at large-DB scale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pane stays responsive during refresh:** a default-view refresh does not block the TUI event loop for more than ~200 ms of perceived lag in aggregate (verified with an automated test harness or measured timing on a large fixture DB) — keystrokes/commands process promptly while a refresh is in flight. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Single-figure refresh cost on large DBs:** a default-view refresh end-to-end (event → data load → render) is bounded to ≤ ~1.5 s wall-clock p95 on a DB of ~2,600 items / ~100 MB, including per-expand child fetches; the consolidated `wl worklist` single-read path stays the norm — no regression to multi-spawn refreshes. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Auto-sync cannot stall the pane:** while a long `wl sync` (measured ~36 s on the 100 MB DB) is in flight in the background, the pane remains responsive — no lock wait, no event-loop stall, at most a brief non-blocking status notice. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Change reflection latency:** after a `wl` write, the pane reflects the change within ~2 s p95 via the event-driven watch path at large-DB scale. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Reduced memory footprint:** a refresh's spawned `wl` processes peak at no more than a documented per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB/spawn observed baseline, OR concurrent spawns are bounded so aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g. ≤ ~300 MB). (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **No regressions:** the full Herdr plugin + TUI test suites pass; the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and event-driven watch semantics are preserved. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)

- All measured numbers are quoted in the completion comment against the F1 baseline; if any criterion is not met, the blocking fix item is referenced with its data rather than accepted silently.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the F1 harness with an end-to-end "all ACs" report mode aggregating
  every metric into one JSON report plus a human summary.
- Drive the event-driven write→reflect measurement at full scale (reusing the
  watch path from WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) and assert AC 4 at large-DB scale.
- Run the full suite + full-scale harness, record the report comment, and mark
  this item (and via parent workflow, the parent) ready once green.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — end-to-end AC report mode.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — metrics under test (spawn/refresh path).
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — in-flight sync scenario under test.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — final numbers.

## Deliverables

- End-to-end AC evidence report (comment + checked-in harness mode), full-suite
  green, and the parent ready for review.

## Dependencies

- F3, F4, F5, F6 (all targeted fixes landed).

# Impl: change-detection persist in db.import / db.importComments

## Background

F2 (WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6) measured the sync persist phase at 83.6 s of an 85.9 s pipeline on the 123.7 MB fixture, with 78–90 % of the CPU inside `upsertFtsEntry`. `db.import()` clears every work item, re-saves every item and then re-indexes the FTS row of every item; `db.importComments()` clears every comment, re-saves every comment and re-indexes the FTS row of every item. A no-change sync therefore pays the whole cost. This item implements the fix behind parent ACs 1, 3 and 4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `db.import()` writes only records whose merged value differs from the local store: unchanged work items/edges/audits are not re-saved, while `updatedAt` preservation and the later-`activityAt` merge still hold (an otherwise identical item carrying a later incoming `activityAt` is still persisted so no activity timestamp is lost).
- Records absent from the incoming full snapshot are still deleted (work items, comments, edges) and only those deleted ids have their FTS rows removed — `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` no longer force a full FTS rebuild, with existing callers (`importData()`, `doctor migrate`, `clear()`) keeping their current destructive behaviour.
- `db.importComments()` writes only changed/new comments and performs FTS upkeep only for the affected parent item ids — FTS maintenance is proportional to changed items, never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge (the delta `upsertComments()` path too: look up only the affected ids instead of scanning every item).
- Each record type is persisted inside one transaction (or batched statements): `db.importComments()` gains a transaction wrapping its clear/save/FTS work, no per-row transaction is introduced, and `db.import()`'s existing atomicity is preserved.
- Existing sync contracts still hold — delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results — and the existing sync and FTS tests plus the write-detection tests from the verification item stay green.

- Change detection: only records whose merged value differs from the local store are written (`saveWorkItem`/`saveComment`/edges/audits); a no-change sync performs zero writes and zero FTS writes.
- FTS maintenance is proportional to CHANGED items (per-changed-item `upsertFtsEntry` or one batched/transactional re-index), never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge.
- Records are persisted in one transaction (or batched statements) per record type — no per-row transaction — and the existing sync contracts still hold: delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results. Existing sync and FTS tests stay green.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `import()`, `importComments()`, `upsertItems()`, `upsertComments()`, `hasWorkItemChanged`/`compareTrackedFields`, `mergeAuditsNewestWins`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `upsertFtsEntry`, `clearWorkItems`, `clearComments`, `saveComment`, `saveWorkItem`, `transaction`.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `performSync` persist branch (delta via `upsertItems`/`upsertComments`, full snapshot via `import`/`importComments`).

## Dependencies

- Verify item (persist write-detection regression tests) — test-first.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `import()`: compute the diff against the existing snapshot — unchanged records (per `hasWorkItemChanged`) are skipped entirely (no `saveWorkItem`), changed/new records are saved, ids absent from the incoming set are deleted with only their FTS rows removed; keep the transaction and `updatedAt`/`activityAt` semantics.
- In `importComments()`: diff comments by identity fields, skip unchanged saves, delete removed comments, wrap clear/save/FTS in one transaction, and re-index FTS only for the affected parent ids.
- Reduce `upsertComments()` to look up only the affected parent ids (no full table scan) and confirm no full FTS rebuild remains after a comment merge.
- Preserve `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` for their remaining callers; introduce targeted FTS-row deletion for the sync path.

## Deliverables

- Rewritten persist path: writes and FTS work proportional to actually-changed records, transactions per record type, contracts unchanged.
data.title: Impl: change-detection persist in db.import / db.importComments

# Impl: sync phase-timing observability

## Background

The F2 stage harness replays `performSync`'s persist pipeline out of process because `wl sync` reports a single wall-clock number with no phase attribution. Parent AC 5 requires the pull/persist/export/push timings to be observable so a before/after breakdown can be reproduced with the documented commands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `performSync` reports per-phase timings for pull, persist-items, persist-comments, export and push as log lines and/or added `--json` fields.
- The F2 probe (`packages/herdr/test/perf/wl-sync-phase-probe.ts`) uses the same phase names, so its output lines up with the in-CLI timings and the before/after table.
- A default-suite test asserts the timing fields/log lines are emitted (present and numeric) and that the existing `--json` sync response shape is unchanged apart from the added timing fields.
- Timing output is off/silent by default where it would pollute machine-readable output (added `--json` fields only, or verbose-only log lines), matching existing `wl sync` output conventions.

- Phase timings are observable (log lines and/or `--json` fields for pull, persist-items, persist-comments, export, push) so the F2 stage harness can reproduce a before/after breakdown with the documented commands.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `performSync` phase boundaries and `--json` output.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/wl-sync-phase-probe.ts` — phase names to align with.
- `packages/herdr/src/wl-sync-phase-probe.test.ts` — probe phase coverage test.

## Dependencies

- Implementation item (change-detection persist) — phases are timed on the rewritten persist path.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a small phase-timer helper in `performSync` around the existing phase boundaries (pull, persist-items, persist-comments, export, push) that emits `--json` timing fields or verbose log lines.
- Align the probe's phase labels with the in-CLI names.
- Add a default-suite test driving `performSync` (dry-run / copied store) asserting the timing fields appear and the existing JSON response shape is unchanged apart from the additions.

## Deliverables

- Observable phase timings in `wl sync` (log and/or `--json`), aligned with the F2 probe, with a regression test.

# Measure and document: persist perf before/after

## Background

Parent ACs 2 and 6 require proof: the persist phase must drop to ≤ 10 % of the F2 baseline on the 123.7 MB fixture, measured with the documented F2 commands, and the re-runnable commands plus a before/after table must land in the docs. `docs/DATA_SYNCING.md` named by the parent does not exist in this repo, so a `docs/dev/` note is the documentation home (the parent AC allows either), alongside the F2 `wl sync` persist section in `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Persist-phase time on the regenerated 123.7 MB F2 fixture (2,600 items / 26,000 comments) is ≤ 10 % of the F2 baseline (57.4 s → ≤ 5.7 s for in-process `db.import` + `db.importComments`), measured with the documented harness and probe commands; the ratio and CPU-profile self-time shares are quoted (not a single wall number, which is load-sensitive).
- A no-change sync profile shows zero `upsertFtsEntry` self time.
- A `docs/dev/` note (e.g. `docs/dev/sync-persist-performance.md`) records the re-runnable commands and the before/after table; the `### wl sync persist phases` section of `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` is updated to record the fix instead of describing it as outstanding.
- The measurements, host context and timestamp are quoted in the parent item's completion comment.

- Persist-phase time on the 123.7 MB F2 fixture drops to ≤ 10 % of the F2 baseline (57.4 s → ≤ 5.7 s in-process `db.import` + `db.importComments`), measured with the documented F2 commands and quoted in the completion comment.
- Docs updated (`DATA_SYNCING.md` and/or a `docs/dev/` note) with the re-runnable measurement commands and the before/after table.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — F1 fixture generator / F2 stage profile.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/wl-sync-phase-probe.ts` — persist-phase probe.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — F2's `wl sync` persist section.
- `docs/dev/sync-persist-performance.md` — new note (before/after table + commands).

## Dependencies

- Implementation item (change-detection persist) and the phase-timing item — the measurement needs both.

## Minimal Implementation

- Regenerate the F2 fixture (`large-db-harness.ts --profile full --stages --json`) and run the persist-phase probe before/after on disposable copies; record wall and CPU times plus `node --cpu-prof` self-time shares.
- Write `docs/dev/sync-persist-performance.md` with the commands and before/after table; update the F2 section in `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`.
- Quote the before/after ratio and CPU shares in a comment on the parent item.

## Deliverables

- Verified ≤ 10 % persist-phase result (or documented blocker if the target is not met), docs update, and parent completion comment with evidence.

## Problem

On the night of 2026-10-22/23 almost **no work was dispatched** by the downtime dispatcher (one work item + one scheduled prompt in ~9 hours, vs 14–15 ContextHub dispatches per night on Oct 20/21). The local LLM was effectively never idle enough to pass the dispatcher's idle/capacity gate.

The cause: a handful of long-running, **operator/manually-triggered** agent panes held the shared local model continuously, each running **9.5–17.5 hours** and still `agent_status: working` this morning:

| Pane started (local) | Item | Kind | Uptime at inspection |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 22 19:27 | WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W (Herdr implement, ⚠️) | implement | 13.5 h |
| Oct 22 15:30 | MS-0MUYK064P0032374 (tce-main-street) | implement | 17.5 h |
| Oct 22 15:33 | MS-0MVCRQ475009CDZI (tce-main-street audit, 🚫) | audit | 17.5 h |
| Oct 22 23:32 | SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS (SorraAgents, 🚫) | implement | 9.5 h |

Their pi session logs confirm continuous local `code`/`plan` model usage through the night (the ContextHub one peaking 03:00–05:00Z), while the retained decision log showed 66 capacity refusals in 84 minutes (`capacity-saturated` 29, `slots-unavailable` 29, `prefill-cap` 2, etc.) with both slots in `decode`, `freeSlots: 0` and prefill serialised at `1/1`.

Key config context: `paneCloseEnabled: false` in `worklog-plugin.json`, so nothing reaps these panes; the non-terminal cooldown and stall-resume scan do not apply to panes that stay `working`.

## Why it matters

- A still-`working` pane that never reaches a terminal stage or a blocked/steady state is invisible to every recovery mechanism (stall-resume, non-terminal cooldown, pane reaper), yet it can monopolise **all** local-LLM slots for 12+ hours and starve the whole fleet's downtime dispatch.
- No alert surfaces while this happens — the dispatcher NOPs by design (`capacity-saturated` etc. are non-terminal), and the decision log rotates in ~1 hour.
- Multi-hour single sessions also collide with the serialised prefill gate (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), turning the scheduler's effective budget to 0 for other work even when one slot is technically idle.

## Goal

As an operator, I want confidence that long-running local-LLM sessions are working productively rather than silently strangling the fleet, and (if they are not) I want them surfaced, recoverable, and — failing that — for the starvation to be visible instead of silent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — For each of the four panes identified above, a comment records the outcome of triage: was the pane productively working (evidence: stage/claims advanced, commits/tests emitted) or stuck in a loop? Each pane is either cleaned up (closed/reassigned) or explicitly justified.
- [ ] AC2 — The stall/stuck-pane detection (or a new guard) can flag a pane whose item **has not progressed** within a documented window (e.g. no stage/status change, no commit) even when `agent_status` is `working` — without requiring `status = blocked/steady`. Verified by tests.
- [ ] AC3 — When the machine-wide local-LLM capacity is continuously refused for dispatch (e.g. `capacity-saturated`/`slots-unavailable`/`prefill-cap`) for a configurable window (default suggestion: 2–3 h), a visible, documented signal is produced (log marker, coordination entry, work item, or TUI notice) — so a silent NOP night becomes discoverable. Tested.
- [ ] AC4 — Documentation note in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` describing the interaction: serialised prefill (`max_concurrent_prefills: 1`) + multi-slot sessions can hold effective dispatch budget at 0, and what operational levers exist (raise prefill concurrency, close/reap sessions, per-slot lease caps).
- [ ] AC5 — Regression test asserting the dispatcher's reason/token stream remains parseable and that no new terminal reason regresses to a silent NOP.

## Evidence

- Fleet `downtime-dispatches.log` tails (2026-10-22/23): only SA `20:04Z` implement, RISE `20:25Z` plan, WL-0MVK3WRY9009KV6P intake `23:26Z`; scheduled `/skill:refactor` `03:12Z`, `/skill:standup` `06:45Z`.
- `ContextHub/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` retained window: 66 no-dispatch decisions, all capacity/prefill/idle refusals; `freeSlots: 0` in 55/66; every tick `prefillsInFlight: 1, maxConcurrentPrefills: 1`.
- Live proxy at investigation time (07:13Z): both slots `generating (decode)`, 0 free, 2–3 `prefill_gate_waiters`.
- pi session logs (`/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/...`) for the four panes show model use across the night.
- `model-cooldowns.json`: SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81 plan pane `w45:pK4` cooldown until `2026-10-23T02:23:54Z` reason "provider exhaustion".
data.title: herdr: long-running agent panes monopolise local-LLM slots and starve downtime dispatch overnight (investigate)

# F8 — Bound the pane's cold spawn fan-out inside the ≤300 MB ceiling at full scale

## Background

F5 (`WL-0MVJV2PC2008PY64`) documented a concurrent read-spawn cap of **2** and
claimed the aggregate spawn-RSS bound `cap × per-spawn peak` stays inside the
parent's ≤ ~300 MB per-pane ceiling ("~220–227 MB"). That claim was measured on
the **tsx** (`src`) target with a warm-ish `wl show` burst (~110 MB/spawn).
F7's end-to-end verification run on the **built** CLI (`dist`, the thing
`/usr/local/bin/wl` runs) at the operator's real scale (2,600 items / 123.7 MB)
measured a **cold `wl show` burst peak of 144.6–175.3 MB per spawn**, so
`2 × peak = 289–351 MB` — and the 175 MB case breaches the 300 MB ceiling
(`runSpawnConcurrencyScenario` reports `aggregate spawn-RSS bound 347.8 MB >
300 MB`, `ok: false`). The cold peak varies run-to-run (144.6–175.3 MB), so a
cap of 2 cannot *guarantee* the documented ceiling.

The parent AC 5 permits either a per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB
baseline OR bounded concurrency inside the documented ceiling. Route (a) is not
available without a payload/memory redesign; route (b) must hold for the
worst-case spawn the pane can issue, not just the refresh's `wl worklist` read.

## Target outcome

The documented spawn cap guarantees the ≤ ~300 MB aggregate ceiling for the
worst-case cold read on a large DB, with the measured bound recorded and
asserted at full scale on the built CLI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documented concurrent read-spawn cap guarantees `cap × worst-case cold
  per-spawn peak ≤ the documented pane ceiling (300 MB)` at full scale on the
  `dist` target, including the cold `wl show` burst scenario (measured, not
  assumed).
- `runSpawnConcurrencyScenario` at full scale on `dist` reports `ok: true`
  (aggregate bound and event-loop blocking inside their documented budgets)
  and the measured numbers are recorded in `large-db-budget.json` /
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`.
- The fallback/fan-out latency trade-off is documented (serialised reads cost
  wall time; the consolidated single-read default view and the in-process
  expand/hydrator reads are unaffected).
- No regression: default-suite spawn-cap, large-DB ratchet, refresh-budget and
  expand/hydrator suites stay green; the consolidated one-`wl worklist`-read
  per refresh and zero-spawn-when-idle guarantees are unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- Lower `DEFAULT_WL_SPAWN_CAP` from 2 to 1 in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
  (the FIFO semaphore already supports it) and update its documentation to the
  measured worst-case bound.
- Update `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-budget.json` (`acTargets.wlSpawnCap`)
  and the F5/F7 documentation numbers; keep the cold-burst assertion.
- Adjust the spawn-cap tests' documented constant expectation.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `DEFAULT_WL_SPAWN_CAP`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-spawn-cap.test.ts` — cap contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/large-db-spawn-cap.test.ts` — measured budget ratchet.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-budget.json` — documented cap.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — measured bound.

## Deliverables

- Measured, asserted full-scale bound inside the 300 MB ceiling; docs updated;
  default suite green.

## Dependencies

- F5 (`WL-0MVJV2PC2008PY64`) — the cap mechanism this tightens.
- Discovered from F7 (`WL-0MVJV2QHO003K6H3`); blocks F7's AC 5 verdict.
